## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
No trials have run yet, so no deviation is ruled out. The starting net scored 0 here. In 6 of 7 earlier worlds every trial scored 0, so this world probably differs from its description. Only the layout-hedged reference net ever scored (about 0.22, world 2). Round 1 therefore follows the program: the reference net, then single-change hedges that each target one possible deviation (action layout and symmetry, footprint or anchor reach, DONE index, obs frame), plus a combined hedge. One planned bet is replaced. Reordering the obs channels cannot matter to a net whose first layer is a 1x1 conv over all channels, so that slot tests obs-frame variants instead. Every file sets K = n_place/(Y·X) instead of assuming n_types. This hedges an action space with extra dimensions, such as a layer index. If n_place is not divisible by Y·X, each file falls back to a learned Linear embedding of the mask. All candidates use the reference recipe.

### Round 2
Every round-1 trial scored 0 on dev. The one nonzero training success was the 5x5 head (0.0006, about one episode), so it is the only lead and may be noise. These deviations are ruled out: (1) the 8 grid symmetries of the action layout, with type-major or type-minor order (r1c2); (2) DONE placed first (r1c4); (3) the whole obs transposed or flipped (r1c5); (4) obs channel order, which the 1x1 stem can learn. The parameter counts also show Z=6, n_types=4 and n_place divisible by Y·X, so the reshape path was used and compact indexing is ruled out. Still possible: anchor or footprint offsets wider than a 3x3 view, dynamics that need non-local information, an arbitrary permutation of action indices, a weak credit signal for the +1 exact-build bonus at gamma 0.9, and too few samples. Each candidate makes one change to the 5x5 net, except one that combines them.

### Round 3
After 12 trials, dev success is 0 everywhere. Training success is 0 too, apart from r1c3's 0.0006, which round 2 could not reproduce and is likely noise. These results rule out the following as the sole deviation: the 16 action layouts (8 symmetries times type-major or type-minor order); DONE at index 0; anchor or footprint offsets within about ±2 cells; whole-obs transpose and flips; a slow dense action remap; and the lack of global context, short horizon or too few samples. The 1x1 stem already learns any permutation of obs channels. So the untested deviations are: (1) the obs stored in a different memory layout, for example channel-minor (Y,X,C) read as (C,Y,X); (2) any fixed scramble of the obs or mask, which only dense embeddings can undo; (3) rotations of channel groups relative to each other, which needs the full 8-symmetry obs hedge; (4) dynamics that need layer-wise reasoning. This round tests (1)-(4), with one sample-count variant on the memory-layout bet.

### Round 4
After 18 trials every dev score is 0. Training success is 0 everywhere except r1c3 (0.0006), and its round-2 refinements also scored 0, so that was noise. Ruled out: the 16 action layouts (8 grid symmetries, type-major or type-minor), DONE first with 4 layouts, flips, transposes and rotations of the obs or its channel groups, channel-last obs, small anchor offsets (5x5 head, dilated conv), global context, longer horizon, more samples (1 epoch), dense input scrambles and the layer-wise encoder. Since many 1x1 nets learn channel permutations, geometry is unlikely to be the problem. Three gaps remain. First, a fully reversed action index: DONE first plus a 180° turn, never tested together. Second, actions numbered only over valid anchors for each brick type. Third, an obs or reward scale that breaks training: a large value loss would dominate the gradient clip and the shared trunk. This last round tests each bet alone, then combined, with one combined net on a 1-epoch recipe.
